title: Convolution, stencils, and implicit GEMM
brief: Compute conv output shapes and halo overhead, lower a convolution to im2col and to an implicit-GEMM index map, and fuse conv, ReLU, and maxpool, all on the CPU. Then write a tiled CUDA conv2d with a constant-memory filter and a z-coarsened 3D stencil. The CUDA checks skip on a machine without a GPU.
hints: conv_out_size is (size + 2 * padding - dilation * (kernel - 1) - 1) // stride + 1. PyTorch floors the division.

The input-tile strategy loads block x block elements and writes only the (block - k + 1) squared threads that have a full neighbourhood. The output-tile strategy loads (tile + k - 1) squared elements and writes tile squared.

halo_tile must give zeros for any coordinate outside the tensor, including negative ones. A negative index in torch or Python wraps to the far edge instead of failing, which is the bug the check looks for.

F.unfold orders the rows of the lowered matrix as channel, then filter row, then filter column: row = c * kh * kw + i * kw + j. Take strided slices of the padded input, one per filter tap, and stack them.
PyTorch convolution does not flip the filter. It computes cross-correlation, so the lowered GEMM is w.reshape(K, C * kh * kw) @ cols with no flip.

In the implicit-GEMM map, m splits into (n, p, q) and k into (c, r, s). The input row is h = p * stride - padding + r * dilation. Return None when h or w is outside the image, because that entry is a padding zero.
A stencil built from torch.roll wraps the boundary around the grid. The reference leaves every boundary cell unchanged.

Bias and ReLU commute with max over a pool window, so the fused version takes the running max of one GEMM per window offset and adds the bias and applies ReLU once. max_pool2d drops a partial window at an odd edge.
The CUDA checks compile with nvcc the first time, which takes 30 to 60 seconds. They skip on a machine without a GPU.
